screening_decisions.reason: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot of intracervical nitroprusside gel immediately before IUD insertion; primary outcome was self-reported pain with insertion (VAS). Fits RCT and preventive pain criteria.

Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled ibuprofen 800 mg vs placebo 30–45 min prior to insertion; primary outcome self-reported VAS pain at insertion. Meets RCT and preventive analgesia criteria.

Randomized trial of immediate vs delayed bladder emptying (full vs emptied bladder) assessing provider ease and women’s self-reported pain at insertion. Nonpharmacologic preventive technique with insertion pain outcomes.

Randomized open-label active-comparator RCT (intracervical 2% lidocaine injection vs oral ibuprofen) in women without prior vaginal delivery; self-reported pain assessed immediately, 2h, and 6h post-insertion. Meets RCT and preventive pain criteria.

Double-blind, placebo-controlled RCT of 800 mg ibuprofen vs placebo 45 min prior to LNG-IUS insertion; self-reported pain at tenaculum and insertion (VAS). Meets RCT and preventive analgesia criteria.
Double-blind, multicenter RCT of 400 μg vaginal misoprostol vs placebo 3 h prior; assessed insertion pain (VAS). Preventive cervical ripening intervention with pain outcomes. Meets criteria.
RCT in nulliparous women: 400 μg buccal misoprostol vs placebo 90 min prior; patient-reported VAS pain at multiple steps including tenaculum and insertion. Meets RCT and preventive criteria.

Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled RCT for consecutive LNG-IUS insertion (repeat users); sublingual misoprostol vs placebo 3 h prior; patient-reported insertion pain reported. Meets RCT and preventive criteria.
Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled prophylactic ibuprofen 400 mg vs placebo ≥45 min prior to copper IUD insertion; self-reported VAS insertion pain. Meets RCT and preventive criteria.

Single-blind randomized trial in parous women with no prior vaginal delivery: sublingual misoprostol 400 μg + diclofenac vs diclofenac alone 1 h prior; outcomes include insertion pain. Meets RCT and preventive criteria.

Double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled ibuprofen 600 mg vs placebo administered before and after insertion; pain assessed at insertion and up to 3 days (≤6h included). Meets RCT and preventive peri-procedural pain criteria.
Randomized, double-blind clinical trial comparing oral tramadol 50 mg, naproxen 550 mg, and placebo 1 h before insertion; VAS pain during insertion primary. Meets RCT and preventive criteria.
Double-blind RCT in nulliparous women: 400 μg misoprostol vs placebo (buccal) 3–4 h prior; provider ease and patient VAS pain at insertion. Meets RCT and preventive criteria.
Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of intracervical 2% lidocaine gel prior to sounding/insertion; VAS pain at multiple steps (including insertion). Meets RCT and preventive criteria.

Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot of vaginal nitroglycerin gel 30 min prior to LNG-IUS insertion; primary: self-reported pain with cervical passage (VAS). Meets RCT and preventive criteria.
Randomized trial of 1% lidocaine paracervical block vs no local anesthetic; VAS pain at tenaculum, insertion, and 5 min post. Meets RCT and preventive local anesthesia criteria.
Randomized, three-arm trial (2% lidocaine gel, lubricant gel, or no intervention) placed intracervically before insertion; VAS insertion pain measured. Meets RCT and preventive analgesia criteria.

Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot of intrauterine infusion of 2% lidocaine vs saline 3 min prior; self-reported pain at tenaculum and insertion (0–9 scale). Meets RCT and preventive criteria.
Randomized trial in nulliparous women: 400 μg sublingual misoprostol + diclofenac vs diclofenac alone 1 h prior; insertion pain VAS recorded; also ease/dilation. Meets RCT and preventive criteria.

Randomized, double-blind clinical trial: 400 μg vaginal misoprostol vs placebo 4 h prior to insertion in nulligravidas; reduced moderate–severe insertion pain; self-reported pain measured. Meets RCT and preventive criteria.
Randomized aromatherapy (lavender) vs placebo 30 min prior; anxiety and VAS pain after IUD insertion measured; preventive nonpharmacologic intervention with pain outcomes. Meets criteria.

Randomized, double-blind trial of self-administered misoprostol 400 μg vs placebo (vaginal or buccal) 3–4 h pre-insertion; provider ease and patient VAS pain at multiple timepoints. Meets RCT and preventive criteria.

Randomized, placebo-controlled trial of a novel topical lidocaine formulation applied to cervix/uterus before IUD insertion; VAS pain during first 10 minutes post-insertion; analgesic efficacy primary. Meets RCT and preventive criteria.

Prospective, single-blinded controlled study with paracervical 1% lidocaine, placebo, or no treatment; VAS pain at tenaculum, insertion, and 5 min. Randomization not explicit—include with caution for full-text verification.
Randomized clinical trial of 400 μg misoprostol vs placebo prior to insertion in nulliparous women; primary outcome: pain at insertion (VAS). Meets RCT and preventive criteria.

Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial: self-administered 2% vaginal lidocaine gel vs placebo 5 min pre-insertion; primary change in VAS pain at insertion; also tenaculum and sounding assessed. Meets RCT and preventive criteria.
Technique/opinion piece on intracervical anesthesia; not a randomized controlled trial of a preventive intervention.

Clinical trial with random assignment to lavender aromatherapy vs sesame oil vs control prior to insertion; VAS pain assessed immediately after insertion; preventive nonpharmacologic intervention. Include pending confirmation of randomization details.
